facts.fact: tech.africa, citing bgp.tools and PeeringDB on 10 August 2026, reports GIXA (Ghana Internet Exchange Association) in service in Accra since 2013 with 24 connected networks on 27 routers.
tech.africa, citing bgp.tools and PeeringDB on 10 August 2026, reports Accra-IX in service in Accra since 2023 with 22 connected networks and 525 Gbps of connected port capacity.
tech.africa, citing bgp.tools and PeeringDB on 10 August 2026, reports LINX Accra (a LINX fabric registered in mid-2025) in service with 8 connected networks and 171 Gbps of port capacity.

Traffic: 200 Gbps (aggregate, operator's own figure announced 10 August 2026, against 525 Gbps of connected ports) at Accra-IX on 2026-08-10; the article notes no public traffic graph exists and that connected ports are not traffic.
Google and Akamai connect at GIXA in Accra, and nowhere else in Accra, per bgp.tools and PeeringDB data of 10 August 2026; Meta is also present there.
Fastly connects at Accra-IX only, and Meta is present on a 100 Gbps port there, per bgp.tools and PeeringDB data of 10 August 2026.
Meta is present at LINX Accra, mostly through a single 100 Gbps port, per bgp.tools and PeeringDB data of 10 August 2026.
GVA of Cote d'Ivoire holds one of four 100 Gbps ports at Accra-IX, as seen in public routing data in August 2026, so a network from another country is a member there.
